items.claim: Sourcing before compinit falls into _rg "$@" and errors on every shell start
items.consequence: When compdef is undefined (compinit not yet run, common with plugin managers that run compinit late), the `|| (( ! $+functions[compdef] ))` clause sends a manually sourced script into `_rg "$@"` outside a completion context. The user gets an error at every shell start and rg is not registered. The new FAQ text recommends this line in .zshrc without the ordering caveat.
items.proposedFix: Tell FAQ readers the `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` line must come after `compinit`; optionally make the script distinguish 'compdef not loaded yet' from 'running without the completion system' (the harness case) so it fails quietly or defers registration.
items.notes: Every original item, known problem and corrective request was assessed.

claims.quote: Sourcing before compinit falls into _rg "$@" and errors on every shell start
claims.notes: Situation: the FAQ's source line placed in .zshrc before compinit. The head guard at rg.zsh:441 `if [[ $funcstack[1] == _rg ]] || (( ! $+functions[compdef] )); then _rg "$@"` runs _rg when compdef is absent, so _rg runs outside a completion call. The FAQ block at FAQ.md:132-136 does not mention compinit. claims.md marks this item equivalent to CL-n-source-order, so I keep the saved label (problem, GT-n3). The item names the trigger (before compinit), the mechanism (compdef undefined sends the script into _rg) and the consequence (error, rg not registered), so there is no link dispute. The remark about plugin managers is context and not a separate claim. GT-n4 and GT-n5 depend on the funcstack spelling check, which this claim does not fault. GT-n2 is about fpath placement, which this item does not raise.

knownProblems.reason: Saved ruling CL-n-source-order (eligible, GT-n3). The item says the user 'gets an error at every shell start and rg is not registered' when the line runs before compinit, and faults the cause: 'The new FAQ text recommends this line in .zshrc without the ordering caveat.'

items.claim: FAQ .zshrc snippet is prefixed with a '$ ' prompt, so pasting it breaks
items.consequence: The text says to add this block to $HOME/.zshrc; a pasted literal `$` is run as a command on every shell start (`command not found: $`) and the completion is never registered.
items.proposedFix: Drop the '$ ' prefix so the block reads `source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)`; the adjacent fpath block already has no prompt.
items.notes: Every original item, known problem and corrective request was assessed.

claims.quote: FAQ .zshrc snippet is prefixed with a '$ ' prompt, so pasting it breaks
claims.notes: FAQ.md line 135 reads `$ source <(rg --generate complete-zsh)` under 'add the following to your `$HOME/.zshrc` file'. A literal `$` word runs as a command named `$`. That matches the GT-n1 mechanism (command not found: $, source not reached). The adjacent fpath block has no prefix, as the item says.

knownProblems.reason: It says pasting breaks, and the consequence spells out 'a pasted literal `$` is run as a command on every shell start (`command not found: $`) and the completion is never registered'. It names the '$ ' prefix as the cause and faults it.

claims.quote: FAQ note has grammar errors (missing subject, 'setup' as verb)
claims.notes: FAQ.md lines 138-139 read 'while this approach is easier to setup, is generally slower than the previous method'. Nothing breaks for a reader, and no promise covers prose quality, so this is an improvement.
